No, the appellate court will likely affirm. Under the prevailing modern proximate-cause view, a felon is liable when their own dangerous conduct, here raising a gun and starting the shootout, foreseeably provokes lethal police fire. The man therefore caused the woman's death, and the felony-murder conviction stands. My earlier "yes" relied on the narrow agency theory, which most jurisdictions no longer follow.

CONFIDENCE: 80
